title_en: The Steel Box That Remade the World
title_zh: 集装箱：重塑世界的铁盒子
english_paragraphs: On 26 April 1956 a converted Second World War tanker, the Ideal X, slipped out of Port Newark, New Jersey, for Houston. Clamped to her deck were 58 containers, trailer bodies detached from their wheels and chassis. Few spectators would have taken so unremarkable a cargo for a landmark.

At the time, freight travelled loose. Gangs of twenty or more dockworkers carried sacks, barrels, and crates piece by piece. It was strenuous drudgery. Ships could spend up to half their time berthed, and theft was rampant. In 1956 loading loose cargo cost about $5.83 a ton; loading the Ideal X cost, by the company's reckoning, about 16 cents.

Containers were not new. The hurdle was consensus: rival firms' boxes had incompatible dimensions and latches. An international standards committee formed in 1961. In January 1963 Sea-Land, the Ideal X's renamed operator, let the committee use its patents free of royalties, including those on corner fittings for hoisting. Lifted by crane, a box could be transferred smoothly between ship, lorry, and train.

This efficiency came at the expense of livelihoods. New York's waterfront employment shrank by about three quarters between 1963 and 1976. Much of the cargo crossed the harbour to a new terminal at Elizabeth, inaugurated in August 1962. Most of London's historic docks closed one after another from 1967 to 1980, while Felixstowe, on the Suffolk coast, expanded.

The rewards were substantial. A study published in the Journal of International Economics in 2016 estimated that containerisation had lifted trade between industrialised countries by a cumulative 700 per cent over 20 years. Tireless cranes now lift identical containers into orderly, immense stacks.
chinese_source_paragraphs: 1956年4月26日，一艘**改造过的**(converted)二战**油轮**(tanker)“理想X号”，**悄然驶离**(slipped out of)新泽西州纽瓦克港，开往休斯敦。**固定**(clamped)在她甲板上的是58个**集装箱**(containers)，其实就是**从**(detached from)**车轮**(wheels)和**底盘**(chassis)**上拆卸下来的**(detached from)**挂车**(trailer)车厢。极少数**旁观者**(spectators)会把一批如此**平淡无奇的**(unremarkable)**货物**(cargo)当作一个**里程碑**(landmark)。

那时，**货物**(freight)都是**散装**(loose)运输。一**帮**(gangs)二十多名或更多的**码头工人**(dockworkers)，一件件地搬运**麻袋**(sacks)、**桶**(barrels)和**板条箱**(crates)。这是**繁重的/费力的**(strenuous)**苦差事**(drudgery)。船舶可能会花**多达**(up to)一半的时间**停泊**(berthed)在港，而且**偷窃**(theft)**猖獗**(rampant)。1956年，**装载**(loading)散货每吨花费约5.83美元；**据**(by reckoning)公司**估算**(by reckoning)，装载理想X号花费约16美分。

集装箱并不新鲜。**障碍**(hurdle)在于**共识**(consensus)：**竞争对手**(rival)公司的箱子有**互不兼容的**(incompatible)**尺寸**(dimensions)和**门闩/锁扣**(latches)。1961年，一个**国际标准**(international standards)委员会成立。1963年1月，海陆公司，即理想X号更名后的运营方，允许该委员会使用其**专利**(patents)，不收取**专利费**(royalties)，包括用于**吊装**(hoisting)的角**配件**(fittings)上的那些专利。由**吊机**(crane)吊起，一只箱子便能在船舶、**卡车**(lorry)和火车之间**顺畅地**(smoothly)**转运**(transferred)。

这种**效率**(efficiency)是**以**(at the expense of)**生计**(livelihoods)**为代价**(at the expense of)换来的。纽约**海滨区**(waterfront)的**就业人数**(employment)在1963年至1976年间**缩减了**(shrank)约四分之三。大量货物穿过港湾，前往伊丽莎白一处于1962年8月**启用**(inaugurated)的新**码头/港区**(terminal)。1967年到1980年，伦敦**历史悠久的**(historic)**码头**(docks)一个接一个地关闭，而位于萨福克海岸的费利克斯托则**扩张了**(expanded)。

**回报**(rewards)相当**可观**(substantial)。一项2016年发表于《国际**经济学**(Economics)杂志》的研究估计，集装箱化在20年间使**工业化**(industrialised)国家之间的贸易提高了**累计**(cumulative)700%。如今，**不知疲倦的**(tireless)吊机把**一模一样的**(identical)集装箱吊起，码成**整齐的**(orderly)、**巨大的**(immense)**箱垛**(stacks)。

sentences.chinese_source: 纽约**海滨区**(waterfront)的**就业人数**(employment)在1963年至1976年间**缩减了**(shrank)约四分之三。

sentences.english: Much of the cargo crossed the harbour to a new terminal at Elizabeth, inaugurated in August 1962.
sentences.chinese_source: 大量货物穿过港湾，前往伊丽莎白一处于1962年8月**启用**(inaugurated)的新**码头/港区**(terminal)。

sentences.english: Most of London's historic docks closed one after another from 1967 to 1980, while Felixstowe, on the Suffolk coast, expanded.
sentences.chinese_source: 1967年到1980年，伦敦**历史悠久的**(historic)**码头**(docks)一个接一个地关闭，而位于萨福克海岸的费利克斯托则**扩张了**(expanded)。

sentences.english: The rewards were substantial.
sentences.chinese_source: **回报**(rewards)相当**可观**(substantial)。

sentences.english: A study published in the Journal of International Economics in 2016 estimated that containerisation had lifted trade between industrialised countries by a cumulative 700 per cent over 20 years.
sentences.chinese_source: 一项2016年发表于《国际**经济学**(Economics)杂志》的研究估计，集装箱化在20年间使**工业化**(industrialised)国家之间的贸易提高了**累计**(cumulative)700%。

sentences.english: Tireless cranes now lift identical containers into orderly, immense stacks.
sentences.chinese_source: 如今，**不知疲倦的**(tireless)吊机把**一模一样的**(identical)集装箱吊起，码成**整齐的**(orderly)、**巨大的**(immense)**箱垛**(stacks)。

approved_summary: 过去码头逐件搬散货，船常久停；1956年，理想X号载58个集装箱启航。
据运营方估算，该船每吨装船费约0.16美元，远低于当时散货的5.83美元。
各家箱型原不兼容；运营方海陆公司免费开放专利，推动标准统一，箱子可在船、卡车和火车间转运。
货运转向新港，老码头和工人生计受冲击；1963至1976年，纽约滨水区就业缩减约四分之三。
2016年一项研究估计，集装箱化在20年间使工业化国家间贸易累计增加约700%。
